With @perturbai_tx and @scrippsresearch, a team of thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents worked in parallel, connecting gene-expression results from millions of mouse brain cells with scientific literature in just 32 minutes. We’re now expanding this collaboration to identify new drug targets.

Aging is a multi-scale physiological process that we can’t actually measure directly. Biomarkers are like the blind men touching the elephant; able to know a piece, but never the whole.

The processes that dictate aging exist at multiple levels of biological complexity. They interact dynamically at different timescales, across different contexts, and along their own trajectories. 

Aging manifests differently among people, but in highly nuanced and often invisible ways. The static, cross-sectional measures the field is used to can only get us so far.

N-of-1 initiatives like mine can capture some of this nuance, but ultimately fails at generalizability. The authors also critique N-of-1 as able to show "responsiveness but not durability; optimisation but not causality."

The challenge, so far unmet, is modelling the complexity of aging in such a way that the output is not a forecast of biomarkers, but a simulation of aging system dynamics, i.e. one’s health trajectory into the future.

The most intriguing implication of such a model is an improved ability to predict how our decisions will impact us in the future. A choose your own adventure where we can predict the consequences of both our healthy and unhealthy behaviors.

This is exactly what we are aiming to build. If you're into this as well, hit me up.

But beyond those claims, something more practical is happening.

𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜 𝗶𝘀 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮 𝗳𝘂𝗹𝗹 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗔𝗜 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗲𝘅𝗲𝗰𝘂𝘁𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸.

Here's how the ecosystem fits together.

𝗔. 𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗔𝗜 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹𝘀

• GPT-6 Astra: Flagship model for complex reasoning, coding, computer use, cybersecurity, and science.

• Benchmark scores: 98% on FrontierMath Tier 4, 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3, and 100% on ExploitBench.

• GPT-6.1 Sol: Near-Astra capabilities at a lower API cost.

• GPT-6 Sol and Luna: Models optimized for different capability, speed, and cost requirements.

𝗕. 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗙𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗲𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 & 𝗧𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀

• Responses API: Combine reasoning, tool calls, and multistep workflows.

• MCP: Connect agents to external tools and enterprise systems.

𝗖. 𝗔𝗜 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘀 & 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗲

• Codex: Handles software engineering tasks, from writing code to testing.

• ChatGPT Agent: Performs research and multistep tasks using browsers and connected tools.

• ChatGPT Work: Executes workflows across business applications, documents, and data.

• ChatGPT Images: Generates and edits visual content.

𝗗. 𝗩𝗼𝗶𝗰𝗲 & 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲 𝗔𝗜

• Realtime API: Enables low-latency voice agents and interactive applications.

𝗘. 𝗠𝗲𝗺𝗼𝗿𝘆 & 𝗚𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲

• Persistent memory: Retains useful context across conversations.

• Preparedness Framework: Evaluates frontier AI risks, including cybersecurity capabilities.

• Safety monitoring: Detects risky behavior and unauthorized actions.

Notably, Astra became OpenAI's first model to reach the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold.

𝗙. 𝗗𝗲𝗽𝗹𝗼𝘆𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 & 𝗣𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗴

• Availability: OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, and AWS Bedrock.

• Standard API pricing: $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗲𝘀?

The value of AI is moving beyond generating responses.

It's increasingly about agents that can research, write code, operate applications, access enterprise knowledge, and complete workflows.

But greater autonomy also requires stronger access controls, monitoring, and human oversight.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗸𝗲𝘆 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆
